cases.note: names compare without case and come back in lowercase, and so do names inside CNAME, MX and SOA data; addresses keep their case
a name with nothing of its own but records below it exists: no data, not a name error
the SOA in a negative answer carries the smaller of its TTL and its MINIMUM field; asked for directly, it keeps its own TTL
an alias answers every type with its CNAME; the closest of a server's zones answers
a zone covers its name and the names that end with a dot and its name, not every name that ends with its letters; an unknown server refuses
records of one name and type come back sorted by their data, without duplicates; the zone's own NS records are an answer
a chain of 8 CNAME records is followed; a ninth makes it too long
a CNAME to itself is a loop; asking for the CNAME type is not followed; a chain can end in no data
a chain may cross zones held by the same server; a negative answer at the end of a chain carries the SOA of the last name's zone
a loop that comes back in different case is still a loop, found when the chain returns to any of its names, not only the first
a chain that leaves the server's zones ends there with NOERROR; without a CNAME, follow answers as lookup does, refusal included
a loop of nine names: the ninth CNAME both closes the loop and exceeds the limit
a cached answer counts its TTL down and is gone when it reaches zero; the referrals stay cached longer
a delegation without glue: the resolver first resolves the server's address from the root, then asks it
a server address that does not answer is skipped, and the next address of the zone is asked
a server that refers back up instead of closer to the name is ignored like one that does not answer, and the next server is asked
addresses and NS records learned from a referral find servers but are never returned as answers
glue for a sibling name inside the parent zone is used, so no extra lookup is needed
when no server of a zone answers, the resolution fails; an address shared by two server names is asked once
a CNAME loop across servers is found by the resolver as well
a cached CNAME is followed from the cache, and only the expired part of the chain is asked again
two delegations whose servers are named in each other's zone, without glue: the resolver does not start a lookup it is already doing, and fails
the TTL is the number of seconds an answer may be used: at 60 seconds a TTL of 60 has run out
servers whose addresses are known are asked before a server name that would need a lookup, even when that name sorts first
a negative answer lasts the SOA's TTL or MINIMUM, whichever is smaller, and then is asked again
no data is remembered for one type only; other types of the name are still asked
a name error at the end of a chain is remembered for the last name, and the chain is replayed from the cache
glue for a name outside the referring zone is never cached, so it cannot redirect later lookups
a name with records below it gives no data, remembered for that type only, not a name error
the negative cache lists name error entries as * and no data entries by type, sorted, with their remaining time
when the real address of an out-of-zone server is already cached, the bad glue is ignored and nothing is looked up again
the negative TTL is the TTL of the SOA row in the response, here 60, smaller than the MINIMUM of 300
